newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Turkmenistan says feuding Afghans ready for peace.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan says feuding Afghans ready for peace.

text.p: Turkmenistan's Vice Premier and Foreign Minister Boris Shikhmuradov said on Sunday he believed warring Afghan factions were ready for peace.
"I have a feeling that all Afghans are prepared for a peaceful settlement," the official Pakistani news agency APP quoted Shikhmuradov as saying after a two-day visit to Pakistan.
He said all Afghan factions should come to the negotiating table because only an intra-Afghan dialogue could bring peace.
The purist Islamic Taleban militia, which controls about two-thirds of Afghanistan, is battling opposition forces on several fronts north of the capital, Kabul.

Shikhmuradov, who held separate talks with Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and the pro-Taleban ambassador to Islamabad, Shahabuddin Dilawar, on Saturday, said his country had no differences with Pakistan over regional policy. "We have no contradictions with Pakistan over regional and bilateral issues," he said, but made clear Turkmenistan had no immediate plans to follow Islamabad's lead in recognising the Taleban administration as the legitimate Afghan government.

"We fully understand moves initiated by Pakistan," he said, apparently referring to Pakistan's May 25 recognition of the Taleban. "Turkmenistan is a U.N. member and will strictly follow all U.N. rules and regulations," he added.
The United Nations has yet to decide whether Afghanistan's seat at the world body should go to the Taleban, who captured Kabul from then-president Burhanuddin Rabbani in September.

Pakistan recognised the Taleban shortly after the militia moved into the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif in alliance with ethnic Uzbek troops who had mutinied against northern opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
The new allies swiftly fell out and the Uzbek troops linked up with Shi'ite Moslem fighters to drive the Taleban from the city after battles that cost the Taleban at least 300 dead.

Shikhmuradov said Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan and other regional nations had agreed to work together for peace in Afghanistan at last month's summit meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation in the Turkmen capital, Ashgabat.

He said he planned to visit Tehran soon for talks with Iranian leaders on the Afghan issue. The Pakistani foreign minister said he planned to visit Turkmenistan and other central Asian states from June 18 to 20.

Khan, who discussed Afghanistan with visiting Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Viktor Pasuvalyuk in Islamabad on Saturday, is also scheduled to visit Moscow on July 7. He told reporters he hoped to allay what he called Russian misgivings about the Taleban, saying neighbouring states had nothing to fear from the fundamentalist Islamic militia.
